@graph.name: How to Hire a Senior Node.js Developer
@graph.description: A step-by-step guide to hiring a senior Node.js developer for your project — from defining requirements to first commit.

step.name: Define your backend requirements
step.text: Identify: REST vs. GraphQL, real-time features (WebSockets/SSE), job queues (BullMQ), framework preference (NestJS for enterprise, Express for smaller projects), and database (PostgreSQL/MongoDB). Write a one-page technical spec before posting.

step.name: Vet for TypeScript and NestJS experience
step.text: Review the candidate's GitHub for TypeScript projects. Look for NestJS module structure, Prisma migrations, and actual Jest test files. Repos without TypeScript from a 'senior' candidate are a red flag. Check for BullMQ or Celery usage — background job experience separates juniors from seniors.

step.name: Assign a paid technical test
step.text: Give a 2-hour paid test: build a NestJS REST endpoint with JWT auth, Prisma query, request validation (class-validator), and a Jest test. This reveals code quality, TypeScript usage, and testing habits without a lengthy interview process.

step.name: Discuss architecture in a call
step.text: Ask: How would you scale this Node.js API to 50,000 req/min? A senior developer discusses horizontal scaling, Redis caching, connection pooling, event loop optimization, and Kubernetes HPA. A junior says 'add more servers'.

step.name: Agree on contract and milestones
step.text: Use milestone-based contracts for fixed-price projects: Discovery/OpenAPI spec → Core API → Auth + Auth → Background jobs → Testing → Deployment + Handover. Each milestone has written acceptance criteria and a payment tied to approval.

step.name: Set up communication and handover process
step.text: Agree on communication channel (Slack/WhatsApp), update cadence (daily async updates), and code review process (PRs to your GitHub repo). Define the handover: source code to your repository, OpenAPI documentation, deployment runbook, and a 60-min walkthrough call.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Express.js and NestJS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Express.js: minimal, unopinionated Node.js framework. Gives you routing + middleware, nothing else. NestJS: opinionated, enterprise-grade framework with dependency injection, decorators, module system, guards (for auth), interceptors, and Swagger auto-generation. Choose Express for small projects; choose NestJS for larger teams or complex domains.

mainEntity.name: What is BullMQ and why is it important in Node.js projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: BullMQ is the modern successor to Bull — a Node.js job queue backed by Redis. It handles background task processing (emails, file uploads, AI inference), scheduled jobs, delayed jobs, priority queues, and failed job retry. Without a job queue, heavy operations block API response time. BullMQ is essential in almost every production Node.js application.

mainEntity.name: How do you scale a Node.js WebSocket application across multiple servers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Redis Pub/Sub as a shared message broker between Node.js instances. Socket.io has a socket.io-redis adapter that automatically routes messages across instances. Each Kubernetes pod maintains its own WebSocket connections, and the Redis adapter ensures that a message emitted on Pod A reaches clients connected to Pod B.
